This unified approach, however, has been challenged by the principles of relativity, which have led to the development of General Relativity. In such cases, traditional methods like the Fast Multipole Method (FMM) and the Fast Multipole Boundary (FMBC) algorithm are often employed, but they come with their own limitations. In this research, we introduce a novel approach that leverages the principles of the FMM to accelerate the computation of Newtonian potentials over complex domains. Our proposed method builds upon the original FMM framework by incorporating the principles of the FMBC algorithm, which allows for the efficient computation of Newtonian potentials over complex domains. Our results demonstrate that this new approach significantly outperforms existing methods, particularly when applied to large-scale problems.
